name: Shibuya
tagline: Shibuya in 1 minute and Shinjuku in 5 minutes. Served by 10 lines.
summary: The station is in Shibuya City, served by JR Yamanote Line, JR Saikyo Line, Narita Express, JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line, Keio Inokashira Line, Tokyu Toyoko Line, Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line, Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line and Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 19 minutes to Otemachi, 5 minutes to Shinjuku, 1 minute to Shibuya and 21 minutes to Shinagawa. The station stands 15.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 20.7 m. The land around the station rises and falls sharply.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 15.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 10.6 m to 31.3 m, a difference of 20.7 m. These figures were read from the elevation API of the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan at nine points: the station itself and eight compass directions 400 m out.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 2 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 26 clinics and 24 pharmacies. Facilities recorded as hospitals lie at 衣笠眼科, about 95 m away and 湘南美容外科, about 207 m away. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 10 lines serve the station: JR Yamanote Line, JR Saikyo Line, Narita Express, JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line, Keio Inokashira Line, Tokyu Toyoko Line, Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line, Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line and Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 4 lines, Keio runs 1 line, Tokyu runs 2 lines and Tokyo Metro runs 3 lines), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company. Scored out of 100 from the number of lines and the spread of operators, transfer convenience here comes to 100.

neighbours.note: 741 m away in a straight line. It takes 7 minutes longer to reach Otemachi than Shibuya.
1183 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi 3 minutes sooner than Shibuya.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want another route when a line stops
notFor: People who would rather not walk up and down slopes
